what_it_does: Fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) lets a server do useful computations on data that has been encrypted end-to-end, so the server never sees the raw values — a powerful privacy tool. The catch is that FHE operations are extremely slow and work on enormous ciphertexts that consume far more memory than conventional data. Most proposed FHE accelerator chips assume the encrypted data already lives on the chip, glossing over the bottleneck of moving gigabytes of ciphertext across the slow PCIe bus that connects a chip to the host computer's memory. Hypnos addresses this by treating data movement as a first-class concern: it packages FHE operations into compact commands that are aware of what data is where, and pairs this with an on-chip memory management system (analogous to how an operating system pages memory to disk) that keeps the most-needed ciphertext blocks on-chip while deferring others. According to the abstract, this reduces both memory traffic and total execution time, though the exact speedup is inferred from the framing rather than verified from full text.
